newsitem.title: UK: WESTERN REFINERY MARGINS FIRM BUT ASIA STRUGGLES.
newsitem.headline: WESTERN REFINERY MARGINS FIRM BUT ASIA STRUGGLES.

text.p: Refinery profit margins picked up in the West but stayed under pressure in Asia last week, continuing the trend seen last month.
In Rotterdam the squeeze in the gasoline market combined with weak Brent crude saw margins peak at $3.22 a barrel last Wednesday, a nine month high, before easing back under $3 by last Friday.
Profit margins rarely stay above $3 a barrel for long in Rotterdam, mostly staying in the $1.50 to $2.50 range.
The gasoline squeeze ended on Wednesday, triggering a $19 a tonne slide in prices which in turn hit margins.
But the decline in refinery margins, calaculated by Reuters from standard product yields, was tempered by falling Brent, which lost about 80 cents a barrel last week.
In the Mediterranean margins gained last week as refiners anticipated an early resumption of Iraqi exports.
The profit margin for fully upgrading Russian Urals crude ended the week at $2.61 a barrel, the highest level since June despite generally sluigghs oil product markets.
On the U.S. Gulf coast margins also gained ground, showing a steady week-on-week average gain of 18 cents a barrel for refining Brent crude.
Margins on the Gulf coast have been trending upwards this year from breakeven levels to around $2.50 a barrel for Brent and $2 on the domestic West Texas Intermediate grade.

Despite gains in the West, Singapore refinery margins weakened last week. A complex refinery averaged $1.91 a barrel compared to levels well above $5 last spring but this was above low seen last month.
Weak gas oil and gasoline have continued to undermine profits over the past few months despite recent support from naphtha.
